title: Mapping Lab + invocation contract fuzzer for tool <-> legacy function interop
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight 'Mapping Lab' harness and run a fuzz-driven invocation contract tester that exercises OpenAI-style tool descriptors and our legacy function surface. The goal is to enumerate real-world mismatches (naming variants, param schemas, streaming continuations, and edge-case outputs), capture provenance for safe rollbacks, and produce a small runtime facade + recommendations to unify mapping strategies without breaking downstream telemetry or customer expectations.
acceptance_criteria: Mapping Lab can load a corpus of 500+ real invocation samples (internal anonymized corpus) and produce a report of top 50 mismatch classes
Fuzzer finds at least 5 high-confidence edge cases that lead to incorrect tool routing or malformed runtime responses
We have a documented mapping strategy (heuristic rules + canonical table) and a minimal runtime facade that adds invocation provenance headers ('X-Invocation-Map') and preserves original payloads
A PoC PR is merged that implements the facade and a reversible toggle behind a feature flag
Tech/PM/Design review sign-off on human-readable mapping rules and rollback plan
tasks: Design Mapping Lab data model and storage format (CSV + JSONL)
Write fuzzer that mutates tool names, param casing, required/optional flips, nested param renames, and streaming chunk boundaries
Run corpus through fuzzer and generate mismatch taxonomy
Implement runtime facade: lightweight shim that applies mapping table and emits provenance header
Add feature flag and metrics (counts of mappings applied, mapping failures, fallback rates)
Create Confluence design doc and link to PR and dashboards
Run canary on dedicated capacity (small percentage) and validate stability
tech_notes: Prefer non-destructive mappings: never drop unrecognized fields; attach mapping metadata in headers rather than rewriting core payload where possible
Heuristics should be applied in order: stable-id lookup -> exact name match -> tokenized name similarity (snake/camel/kebab) -> semantic alias map -> fuzzy edit-distance fallback
For streaming tool invocations, keep a continuity token in the facade (invocation_map_id) so later chunks can be reconciled to original invocation
Avoid coupling mapping table to business logic: store canonical table in Git (yaml) and load into runtime at startup with TTL for updates
Fuzzer edge-case to prioritize: identical parameter lists but different param semantics (e.g., 'timeout' in ms vs seconds)
decisions: Do not attempt deep semantic conversion (units/enum normalization) in first iteration — surface mismatches in report instead
Feature-flag the facade to allow rapid rollback if customer-visible regressions occur
Telemetry-first approach: log mapping attempts and failures before auto-applying non-deterministic heuristics
Keep canonical table in Git with code review required for changes to prevent silent drift
